text:
Ingrid: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A about our engineering process (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Leaving a short recap and answers.

Lee: Thanks! Two quick clarifications: is the biweekly train still the default, and what does the freeze window look like?

Ingrid: Yes — biweekly release train (Tue 09:00 PT). Freeze = 48h for runtime/serving/model infra. Non-blocking UI changes can land behind feature flags.

Sofia: Oncall ops: 2-week rotations, primary + secondary. Escalation: primary -> secondary -> oncall manager (20m) -> SRE lead. Targets: ack <10m, mitigation/rollback attempt <30m. If hosted customer SLA is affected, notify CS within 1h.

Priya: Canary policy (starter defaults): 5% for 1h -> 25% for 6h -> full if green. Monitor model-quality evals, token-error, user error-rate, latency p95/p99. Auto-rollback triggers include: quality drop >5% on labeled evals, user error rate >2x baseline, or p99 latency +40% (or p95 +200ms) over baseline. ML will tune per-model.

Lee: Where are the runbooks? Ops needs links.

DevBot: Release playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/release-cadence  Canary policy: https://redwood.internal/platform/canary-policy  Incident runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-response

Emily: Rollback authority for incidents 1? Can oncall revert without PM OK?

Ingrid: Yes. Oncall has rollback authority when incident meets severity thresholds in the runbook. Notify PMs ASAP but do not wait for approval.

Priya: We'll publish a short RACI and update the playbook with explicit canary numbers by Friday EOD.

Ingrid: We'll also host a 45-min office hours next Wed 4pm PT to walk the details: https://calendar.internal/event/eng-playbook-qa. Tag me if I missed anything and I'll add it. :thumbsup:
